classification.difficultyReason: Eliminate time using a known point on the trajectory and rearrange to determine the initial speed.

content.prompt:
A projectile was fired from level ground and just cleared a wall $10\text{ m}$ high and $20\text{ m}$ from the point of projection. If the angle of projection was $36^\circ$, find the initial speed to the nearest integer.

Note: the height of the wall is not necessarily the maximum height.

answer.worked:
Let $V$ be the initial speed. Take the point of projection as the origin and use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

$$\begin{aligned}x&=V\cos36^\circ\,t\\y&=V\sin36^\circ\,t-5t^2\end{aligned}$$
At the wall, $x=20$ and $y=10$.

$$\begin{aligned}20&=V\cos36^\circ\,t\\t&=\frac{20}{V\cos36^\circ}\end{aligned}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation:

$$\begin{aligned}10&=V\sin36^\circ\left(\frac{20}{V\cos36^\circ}\right)-5\left(\frac{20}{V\cos36^\circ}\right)^2\\10&=20\tan36^\circ-\frac{5(400)}{V^2\cos^236^\circ}\\\frac{5(400)}{V^2\cos^236^\circ}&=20\tan36^\circ-10\\V^2&=\frac{2000}{\cos^236^\circ(20\tan36^\circ-10)}\\V^2&\approx674.5\\V&\approx26\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$$
The initial speed is $26\text{ m/s}$ to the nearest integer.
